# The retarget payment of fx_invoice_usd_retarget_payment.txt, with a split
# line added to the payment block.
#
# `txn_guid:` claims a transaction that already exists and already carries the
# splits it was written with — including its FX gain. There is no entry here
# for a further split line to join, so the fee below would be placed nowhere.
#
# What this fixture produces: the import is refused, naming the fee and telling
# the writer to put it in the transaction they are attaching. Accepting the
# file and dropping the line would leave the book holding less than it states.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_payment_split_must_be_consumed.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-01-05
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-05
		description: "Consulting"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-05
		due: 2026-02-05
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-02-25
		amount: 100
		account: "Assets:Bank"
		txn_guid: "5a1d9e77c0f04a6cbc3b0d1f2e4a6b8c"
		txn_split_guid: "9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a0"
		memo: "Payment for INV-USD-001"
		Expenses:Bank Fees 2.00 CAD
